3D_Viewpoint.strategy:
To solve the 3D Viewpoint CAPTCHA, begin by reading the on-screen prompt, which instructs you to identify all grid cells showing the exact same 3D wireframe object as the reference, viewed from different angles but with identical edge colors.

First, carefully examine the reference 3D object displayed above the grid. This reference may be rendered as an interactive 3D viewer or a static image. Take note of the object's overall geometric shape (such as a pyramid or a truncated pyramid) and meticulously map out the specific colors assigned to each of its edges. Pay close attention to the spatial relationship between the colored edges, distinguishing between the base edges, lateral edges, and any top edges.

Next, evaluate the grid of option images below. Each cell presents a 3D wireframe from either a side perspective or a top-down view. Your task is to determine which of these views represent the exact same object as the reference. To do this, mentally rotate the reference object or trace the connections between the colored edges to see if they match the arrangement in the cell. Distractor cells will feature the correct geometric shape but will have subtly altered color patterns, such as swapped colors between two edges or a rotated color sequence along the base or sides.

Click on every grid cell that perfectly preserves the original edge color arrangement of the reference object. There will be multiple correct cells to find. As you click, a checkmark will appear over each selected cell. Once you have identified and selected all the matching viewpoints, scroll down and click the "Submit" button to finalize your answer.

Backmost_Layer.strategy:
To solve the Backmost Layer puzzle, start by reading the on-screen prompt to identify the specific target shape you need to find. A reference image of this target shape is also displayed above the grid to help you clearly recognize its outline.

Next, examine the grid of images. Each cell in the grid contains a cluster of three overlapping shapes, each with its own distinct color and pattern. Your task is to determine the depth ordering of these shapes by carefully observing how they overlap.

Look for occlusion cues to figure out which shape is in the front, middle, and back. The frontmost shape will appear whole and cover parts of the other shapes. The middle shape will be partially covered by the frontmost shape but will cover part of the backmost shape. The backmost shape will be partially hidden behind the other two shapes and will not cover any other shape.

Evaluate every cell in the grid to identify its backmost shape. If the backmost shape in a cell matches the target reference shape requested in the prompt, click on that cell to select it. A checkmark or visual indicator will appear to confirm your selection. Continue this process until you have evaluated all the cells and selected every one where the target shape is at the very back of the stack.

Once you have selected all the correct cells, click the 'Submit' button at the bottom of the puzzle area to finalize your answer.

Box_Folding.strategy: To solve the Box Folding puzzle, you must identify which 3D cubes can be correctly formed by folding the provided 2D template. First, read the on-screen prompt to confirm the task and the number of targets you need to find. Next, examine the reference image at the top of the puzzle area. This image displays an unfolded 2D cube net with a distinct symbol on each of its six faces. Carefully analyze the spatial relationships between the symbols on the 2D net. Identify which faces are adjacent and which are opposite. A key rule of cube folding is that faces separated by exactly one square in a straight line on the net are opposite each other and can never be visible simultaneously on the 3D cube. Additionally, note the rotational orientation of each symbol relative to its neighbors—how the "top" of one symbol aligns with the edges of adjacent symbols when the net is folded. Next, inspect the grid of 3D cube options below the reference image. Each option displays a cube with three visible faces. Evaluate each option by checking for impossible configurations: 1. Eliminate any cube that displays two symbols that should be on opposite faces. 2. Eliminate cubes where the visible symbols are adjacent on the net but appear in the wrong spatial arrangement. 3. Eliminate cubes where the symbols are correctly placed but have the wrong rotational orientation (e.g., a symbol is rotated or upside down relative to how it should connect to its neighbor). Find the exact cubes that perfectly match the folded net in both symbol placement and orientation. Click on the grid cells containing these correct cubes to select them; a visual indicator will confirm your selection. Finally, click the "Submit" button to finalize your answer.

Color_Counting.strategy:
To successfully solve the Color Counting puzzle, you must identify and select specific sketch images from a grid based on the number of distinct colors they contain. Begin by carefully reading the text prompt displayed at the top of the puzzle area. This prompt will provide the exact mathematical condition you need to fulfill for the current instance, such as finding sketches with a specific number of colors or fewer, or sketches with more than a certain number of colors. The instructions will also explicitly remind you to ignore the color white during your evaluation.

Next, systematically examine the grid of images provided below the prompt. For every individual sketch, visually scan the drawing and count the total number of unique colors used in its composition. Always exclude white from your final count for each image, as it functions as the background or empty space.

After determining the distinct color count for a given sketch, compare that number against the target condition you read in the prompt. If the sketch's color count satisfies the rule, click on that image to select it. You will see a visual indicator, such as a checkmark or an overlay, confirming your selection. Continue this process until you have evaluated every single image in the grid.

Double-check your work to ensure you have clicked all the sketches that match the criteria and have not accidentally selected any distractors. Once you are confident that all correct images have been chosen, locate and click the "Submit" button at the bottom of the puzzle area to finalize your answer.

Dice_Roll_Path.strategy:
To solve the Dice Roll Path puzzle, your goal is to determine which number will appear on the top face of the dice after it rolls along the designated path. First, read the on-screen prompt to confirm the task. Next, examine the main puzzle image, which displays a 3D grid, a starting dice with visible pips, and a path drawn across the grid cells.

If a reference image is provided in the UI, use it to understand the layout of the dice faces. Standard dice have opposite faces that sum to 7 (e.g., 1 is opposite 6, 2 is opposite 5, and 3 is opposite 4). Using the visible pips on the starting dice and this rule, deduce the numbers on the hidden faces (bottom and opposite sides).

Carefully trace the path step-by-step from the starting cell to the end of the line. For each single-cell movement along the grid (whether up, down, left, or right in the grid's perspective), mentally track the 90-degree rotation of the dice. When the dice rolls one step in a given direction, the current top face rolls down to become the side face in that direction, the previous side face becomes the new bottom, the old bottom rolls up to become the opposite side, and the opposite side becomes the new top. The two faces perpendicular to the direction of the roll remain completely unchanged.

Keep track of the top, bottom, and side faces as you mentally simulate each step of the roll along the entire path. Once you reach the final cell at the end of the path, identify the number of pips that will be facing up. Finally, type this single number into the provided number input field and click the Submit button to complete the puzzle.

Dynamic_Jigsaw.strategy:
To solve the Dynamic Jigsaw puzzle, your goal is to reconstruct an animated image by placing scattered puzzle pieces into their correct positions on a grid. Begin by reading the on-screen prompt to confirm the task.

Next, inspect the webpage UI to locate three main components: the animated reference image (which shows the completed puzzle), the empty puzzle grid, and the tray containing the draggable animated puzzle pieces. Note the dimensions of the grid to understand how many pieces need to be placed.

The key to solving this puzzle lies in observing the animations. Both the reference image and the individual pieces feature moving shapes that travel across the screen. Carefully watch the trajectories, colors, and types of shapes in the reference image. Then, examine the pieces in the tray to find matching movements. Because the shapes move continuously, a shape that exits the boundary of one piece must seamlessly enter the adjacent boundary of the correct neighboring piece.

Click and drag each piece from the tray into its corresponding cell within the puzzle grid. If you make a mistake, you can drag a piece from one grid cell to another to rearrange them, or drag it back to the tray to clear the cell.

Once you have placed all the pieces into the grid, take a moment to watch the combined animation. Verify that all moving shapes transition smoothly and continuously across the grid boundaries, perfectly matching the flow of the reference image. There should be no broken shapes or disjointed movements. When you are confident that the pieces are arranged correctly, click the "Submit Puzzle" button to finalize your answer.

Hole_Counting.strategy:
To solve the Hole Counting puzzle, begin by reading the text prompt at the top of the screen to determine the exact target number of holes you need to find (for example, '2 holes' or '4 holes'). 

Next, examine the grid of images provided below the prompt. Each cell in the grid displays a large, irregularly shaped blob with a specific color and texture pattern, set against a solid background. Your task is to count the number of 'holes' located entirely inside each main shape. 

A hole is defined as a smaller, distinct region that is completely enclosed by the main shape. These holes are designed to be visually striking: they feature a highly contrasting color compared to both the main shape and the background, and they are filled with a very fine-grained texture pattern, such as tiny dots, fine lines, or a tight grid. 

Carefully inspect each grid cell one by one. Count the number of these distinct, textured hole regions enclosed within the main shape. Be careful not to confuse the main shape's own larger texture pattern or the outside background with a hole. 

Click on every image in the grid where the number of enclosed holes exactly matches the target number requested in the prompt. When you click a cell, a checkmark will appear to indicate it has been selected. After you have identified and selected all the matching cells in the grid, click the 'Submit' button located below the puzzle to finalize your answer.

Illusory_Ribbons.strategy:
To solve the Illusory Ribbons puzzle, begin by reading the on-screen prompt to determine the exact target number of ribbons you need to find (for example, exactly 3 or 4 ribbons). The puzzle presents a grid of images, each containing multiple weaving ribbon loops.

Your task is to count the number of distinct ribbons in each grid cell. Keep in mind that each ribbon is a single, continuous closed band. The ribbons may weave over and under one another, and they often feature varying color gradients that can make them visually blend together. To accurately count them, carefully trace the path of each visible ribbon segment, following it as it passes behind other ribbons, until you verify it forms one complete, unbroken loop. Do not rely solely on color to separate the ribbons, as the gradients and overlapping layers are designed to be confusing. Instead, focus on the structural continuity of each loop.

Evaluate every cell in the grid using this tracing method. Once you have determined the total count of separate ribbon loops for a cell, compare it to the target number requested in the prompt. Click on every grid cell that contains exactly the target number of ribbons. A checkmark or visual indicator will appear on the cells you select. After you have identified and clicked all the matching cells in the grid, click the "Submit" button to finalize your answer.

Layered_Stack.strategy: To solve the Layered Stack puzzle, begin by carefully reading the on-screen text prompt to understand the specific counting and layering conditions required. The prompt will specify a particular top shape that must be at the highest layer of the stack, a target shape to look for in the layers beneath it, and the exact number of times that target shape must appear. Next, examine the grid of images, where each cell contains a vertical stack of overlapping shapes (such as circles, squares, triangles, or stars) with various colors and fill patterns. For each cell, first identify the shape at the very top of the stack. You can determine this by looking for the shape that is fully visible and not occluded or overlapped by any other shape. If this top shape does not match the one requested in the prompt, you can ignore the cell. If the top shape does match the prompt's requirement, carefully inspect the partially occluded shapes in all the layers underneath it. Count how many times the specified target shape appears in these lower layers. Pay close attention to the visible edges, corners, and fill patterns peeking out from behind the upper layers to correctly identify and count the partially hidden shapes. If the number of target shapes in the lower layers exactly matches the count requested in the prompt, click on that cell to select it. A checkmark or visual overlay will appear to confirm your selection. Evaluate every cell in the grid using this same process, as there may be multiple correct answers. Once you have selected all the cells that satisfy the prompt's specific layering and counting conditions, click the Submit button to finalize your answer.

Mirror.strategy:
To successfully solve this CAPTCHA, begin by carefully reading the on-screen instructions to determine the exact selection criteria. The prompt will typically ask you to identify specific types of mirror reflections, such as selecting all incorrect mirror images that do not properly match the provided reference object. Next, locate the 'Reference' section on the webpage, which displays the original baseline image you must use for comparison. Below or adjacent to this, you will find an options grid containing multiple candidate images.

Your task is to visually analyze each candidate image in the grid and compare it against the reference image. Mentally or visually simulate a mirror reflection of the reference object and check if the candidate matches this expected reflection. Look closely for subtle discrepancies, such as incorrect spatial arrangements, missing details, asymmetrical features, or structural anomalies that violate how a true mirror reflection should appear.

Once you have evaluated the candidates, click on every image in the grid that satisfies the condition stated in the prompt. Clicking a candidate will visually toggle its selection state, often displaying an overlay or a badge to confirm it has been chosen. Be thorough in your evaluation, as there may be multiple correct images that need to be selected, and you must identify all of them. After you have confidently selected all the matching candidate images, locate the 'Submit' button—typically found below the options grid—and click it to finalize and submit your answer. Do not click submit until you have made all your selections, as you only have one attempt.

Multi_Script.strategy:
To solve this CAPTCHA, start by examining the reference image displayed at the top of the puzzle area. This image shows a set of target characters from various writing systems. Carefully study the unique structural features of each target character, such as the arrangement of dots, specific curves, intersecting lines, or distinct asymmetric shapes.

Next, look at the grid of cells below the reference image. Each cell contains a small cluster of characters. Your task is to identify which cells contain any of the target characters shown in the reference image.

The primary challenge is that the characters inside the grid cells have been visually transformed—they may be rotated at random angles and potentially mirrored (flipped horizontally). Because of these transformations, you cannot rely on the standard upright orientation of the characters. Instead, focus on the intrinsic geometry of each shape. Look for the relative positioning of strokes, the number of dots, and the way lines connect or curve, as these topological features remain consistent even when the character is turned upside down or viewed in a mirror.

Scan through every cell in the grid one by one. Mentally rotate and flip the characters in each cell to see if they match the structural blueprint of any of your target characters. Click on every cell that contains at least one matching character. A checkmark will appear on the cells you select. Once you have thoroughly checked all the cells and selected all the correct ones, click the 'Submit' button at the bottom to finalize your answer.

Occluded_Pattern_Counting.strategy:
To solve this CAPTCHA, begin by carefully reading the on-screen instructions to identify the two specific target combinations of color and shape you are required to count. The image displays a grid of colored shapes, where a portion of the grid is covered by a semi-transparent grey overlay.

Your task is to count the exact number of times each of the two target color-shape combinations appears strictly underneath this grey overlay. Do not try to infer the hidden content by extending the visible pattern from uncovered areas — the arrangement beneath the overlay may differ from what the surrounding pattern would suggest. Instead, look directly through the semi-transparent grey overlay and visually identify and count the actual shapes present in the occluded region.

Once you have determined the true count for both target combinations hidden under the overlay, locate the two number input fields provided on the page. Type the count for the first requested color-shape combination into the first input field, and type the count for the second requested combination into the second input field. Finally, click the 'Submit' button to finalize your answer. Remember, only count the shapes that are located under the grey overlay, and trust your direct visual observation through the transparency rather than inferring based on the surrounding visible grid.

Red_Dot.strategy:
To successfully solve the Red Dot puzzle, you must demonstrate quick reaction times by interacting directly with the visible elements in the puzzle area. Begin by reading the on-screen prompt to confirm your objective, which is typically to click a red dot before it disappears. 

Scan the main puzzle canvas to locate the red dot. Once identified, immediately move your cursor and click directly on the dot. This task is highly time-sensitive; you must execute the click as quickly as possible, as taking too long will cause the puzzle to time out and fail. 

Do not attempt to use the standard 'Submit' button for this task. The puzzle is designed to automatically register your input the moment you click the dot. 

After your initial click, carefully observe the puzzle area. Some variations of this puzzle require multiple sequential successful interactions. If a new red dot appears in a different location within the canvas after your first click, you must quickly locate and click this new dot before its individual timer expires. Continue this process of rapidly locating and clicking any newly appearing red dots until the puzzle concludes. You will know the task is complete when the puzzle area stops displaying new dots and a final result message appears on the screen. Always prioritize speed and precision when interacting with the targets.

Rotation_Match.strategy:
To solve the Rotation Match puzzle, start by reading the on-screen prompt, which instructs you to find and select all instances of the shape that appears most frequently in the grid. 

Next, examine the grid of images. Each cell contains an irregular, distinct geometric shape. These shapes are rendered with various colors, internal patterns (like stripes, dots, or checkerboards), and placed on textured backgrounds. To succeed, you must completely ignore the colors, patterns, and background noise, focusing exclusively on the outer silhouette or outline of the shapes.

Carefully compare the shapes across all cells. The shapes may be rotated at different angles, so you will need to mentally rotate them to determine if their base geometry matches. Group the cells by their underlying shape and count how many times each unique shape appears in the grid. 

Identify the single shape that occurs most frequently (this target shape will typically appear in several cells, while distractor shapes will appear fewer times). Once you have identified the most common shape, click on every grid cell that contains it, regardless of its rotation, color, or fill pattern. A visual indicator, such as a checkmark, will appear on each cell you select. Double-check the grid to ensure you have selected all instances of the target shape and haven't accidentally selected any distractors. Finally, click the 'Submit' button located below the grid to finalize your answer.

Shadow_Direction.strategy:
To solve the Shadow Direction puzzle, start by reading the on-screen prompt to identify the target light direction (e.g., 'TOP LEFT', 'BOTTOM RIGHT', 'RIGHT'). The prompt specifies where the light source is coming from. A reference arrow image is also displayed to help illustrate this direction.

Next, examine the grid of images. Each cell displays a 3D object casting a shadow onto the ground. Apply the basic physics of lighting: a shadow is always cast in the opposite direction from the light source. For example, if the prompt says light comes from 'BOTTOM RIGHT', the shadow will extend toward the upper-left area of the image. If the light comes from 'TOP', shadows will extend downward.

For each cell, observe where the shadow falls relative to the object. Determine which direction the light must be coming from to produce that shadow. If the inferred light direction matches the target direction stated in the prompt, select that cell.

Carefully evaluate every cell in the grid and click on all images where the shadow is consistent with the requested light direction. Once you have selected all matching cells, click the 'Submit' button to finalize your answer.

Shadow_Plausible.strategy:
To solve this CAPTCHA, begin by reading the on-screen prompt to confirm the exact requirement, which typically asks you to identify images featuring physically plausible shadows. 

Next, examine the grid of images presented on the webpage. Your goal is to evaluate the relationship between the objects and the shadows they cast in each scene. For every image, analyze the implied direction of the light source based on the highlights and shading on the objects. Then, check if the cast shadow aligns with this light source in terms of angle and direction. Additionally, verify that the shape and perspective of the shadow accurately reflect the geometry of the object casting it, accounting for the surface it falls upon. Images where the shadow contradicts the light source, has an impossible shape, or points in the wrong direction are incorrect.

Once you have identified the images that display realistic and logically consistent shadows, click on each one to select it. Clicking an image will toggle its selection state, typically displaying a checkmark or a highlight overlay to confirm it has been chosen. Be thorough in your evaluation, as there may be multiple correct images within the grid, and you must select all of them to pass. 

After you have carefully reviewed all the options and selected every matching image, scroll down if necessary to locate the 'Submit' button positioned below the grid. Click this button to finalize and submit your answer. Remember that you only have one attempt, so ensure your selections are complete and accurate before submitting.

Spooky_Circle.strategy:
To successfully solve the Spooky Circle puzzle, you must rely on motion perception rather than static image analysis. Begin by reading the on-screen prompt to confirm your objective, which is to count the number of hidden circles within the provided animation.

Next, focus your attention on the animated media. If you only examine a single static frame, the entire image will appear as uniform, featureless static noise, making the circles completely invisible. Instead, you must watch the animation play out over several seconds. The puzzle uses motion contrast to reveal the targets: the background noise will continuously scroll in one specific direction (for instance, upwards), while the hidden circular regions will scroll in the exact opposite direction (for instance, downwards).

Carefully scan the entire animated area and look for these distinct patches of opposite-moving noise. Because the circles blend perfectly into the background in any frozen moment, their boundaries only become apparent through this contrasting movement. Take your time to track and count every individual circular region that moves against the primary flow of the background. Make sure to scan from edge to edge so you do not miss any circles that might be positioned near the borders or overlapping slightly.

Once you have determined the total number of opposite-moving circles, locate the number input field on the webpage. Type your final count into this field. Finally, click the 'Submit' button to enter your answer. Remember that you only have one attempt, so be certain of your count before submitting.

Spooky_Circle_Grid.strategy: To solve the Spooky Circle Grid puzzle, you must identify specific animated cells based on motion contrast. First, read the on-screen prompt to confirm your objective, which involves finding cells that contain hidden circles. Next, examine the grid of animated images. If you only look at a single static frame, every cell will appear as identical, uniform static noise, and the circles will be completely invisible. To reveal the hidden shapes, you must watch the animations play over time. Focus on the movement within each cell. In empty cells, the noise pattern will scroll uniformly in a single direction. However, in the target cells, you will notice a distinct circular region where the noise scrolls in the exact opposite direction to the surrounding background. This opposite motion creates a 'motion contrast' effect, making the hidden circle visually pop out from the background after a brief moment of observation. Carefully scan the entire grid and click on every cell where you observe this opposite-moving circular region. When you click a cell, a checkmark overlay will appear to indicate it has been selected. Make sure to evaluate every cell in the grid, as there may be multiple targets. Once you have selected all the cells containing the motion-contrast circles, click the 'Submit' button located below the grid to finalize your answer. Do not attempt to guess based on static screenshots; you must rely on the temporal motion of the animations to successfully distinguish the target cells from the empty ones.

Spooky_Jigsaw.strategy:
To solve this motion-based jigsaw puzzle, begin by reading the on-screen instructions to understand the objective. The puzzle interface consists of a reference image, an empty grid, and a tray of puzzle pieces. All of these visual elements are animated images covered in visual noise.

Because the images initially appear as uniform static noise, you must observe the animations over time to see the hidden content. Watch carefully as the noise patterns move: the background noise scrolls in one direction while the hidden shapes scroll in the opposite direction. This contrasting motion reveals the actual content, shapes, and boundaries of the jigsaw puzzle.

Study the animated reference image to understand the complete picture formed by these moving shapes. Then, examine each individual piece in the tray, watching its animation to identify which part of the overall pattern it contains. Compare the moving shapes in each piece to the corresponding sections of the reference image to determine its correct location in the grid.

Once you have identified where a piece belongs, click and drag it from the tray into the correct empty cell in the grid. Repeat this process for every piece in the tray until the entire grid is filled and the combined motion patterns perfectly match the reference image. If you make a mistake, you can drag a placed piece back to the tray or directly into another grid cell to adjust its position. After all pieces are correctly placed in the grid, click the 'Submit Puzzle' button to finalize your answer.

Spooky_Shape_Grid.strategy:
To solve the Spooky Shape Grid puzzle, you must identify specific shapes hidden within animated noise patterns based on their shape type and rotation direction. 

First, read the on-screen prompt carefully to determine your exact targets for the current puzzle. The prompt will specify both a target shape (such as a circle, square, or triangle) and a target rotation direction (either clockwise or counterclockwise). 

Next, examine the grid of animated images. At first glance, the cells may look like random static or noise. However, as you watch the animations over a few seconds, you will notice that a portion of the noise in each cell is rotating. The boundary of this rotating noise forms a distinct shape. 

Focus on one cell at a time. Watch the movement to deduce the hidden shape by observing its outline—look for the smooth, continuous edge of a circle, the four distinct corners of a square, or the three points of a triangle. Once you have identified the shape, observe which way the noise pattern inside it is turning to determine its rotation direction (clockwise or counterclockwise).

Compare the shape and direction in each cell against the specific combination requested in the prompt. You must find the cells that match both criteria perfectly. Be careful to ignore distractor cells that might have the correct shape but are rotating in the wrong direction, or cells that are rotating in the correct direction but feature the wrong shape. 

Click on every grid cell that contains the exact target shape rotating in the specified direction. A visual indicator, such as a checkmark or overlay, will appear on the cells you select. There are typically multiple correct cells in the grid. Once you have selected all the matching cells, click the "Submit" button to finalize your answer.

Spooky_Size.strategy:
To solve the Spooky Size puzzle, begin by reading the on-screen prompt to determine the specific target shape (such as a circle, square, or triangle) and the required size comparison (either the 'smallest' or 'largest'). 

Next, carefully observe the animated image in the puzzle area. At first glance, the image may appear to be just static noise. However, as the animation plays, you will notice several shapes revealed entirely through motion contrast. These shapes rotate continuously against the noisy background, making their outlines and forms visible only while they are moving.

Watch the animation for a few cycles to scan the entire canvas and locate all instances of the requested shape type. Ignore any shapes that do not match the target type, as they are merely distractors. Once you have identified all the rotating shapes of the correct type, compare their relative sizes. Depending on the prompt's instructions, find either the single smallest or the single largest instance among them. 

After you have confidently pinpointed the correct target shape, position your cursor over its center and click directly on it within the animated canvas. The puzzle is designed to automatically record your click coordinates and submit your answer immediately upon interaction. Therefore, you do not need to search for or click a separate 'Submit' button. Wait for the success or failure message to appear to confirm your result.

Spooky_Text.strategy:
To solve this CAPTCHA, begin by reading the on-screen prompt to confirm your objective, which is to identify the hidden text within the provided animation. 

Next, focus your attention on the animated media. It is critical that you observe the animation over time rather than analyzing a single static frame. If you look at any individual frame, the image will appear as completely uniform, unreadable static noise. The text is entirely invisible without motion.

Instead, watch the movement of the noise patterns carefully. The puzzle uses motion contrast to reveal the hidden characters. You will notice that the general background noise scrolls continuously in one specific direction. However, there is a distinct region within the noise that scrolls in the exact opposite direction. 

Pay close attention to the boundaries of this opposite-moving region. The area where the noise moves against the background flow forms the precise shapes of the hidden text, which may consist of letters, numbers, or words. By tracking this contrasting motion over the course of a few seconds, the shapes of the characters will emerge and become readable. 

Once you have successfully read the hidden text by observing the contrasting motion, click on the text input field provided on the webpage. Type the exact characters you identified from the animation into the input box. Finally, click the "Submit" button to finalize your answer. Remember that you must rely on temporal observation—watching the frames play out sequentially—to perceive the text, as static image analysis will yield no visible shapes.

Static_Jigsaw.strategy:
To solve the Static Jigsaw puzzle, begin by reading the on-screen prompt to confirm your objective. Your goal is to reconstruct a complete image by arranging scattered puzzle pieces into a designated grid. 

First, carefully inspect the visible webpage UI. You will see an empty puzzle grid with a specific layout of rows and columns, a tray area below it containing the shuffled puzzle pieces, and a "Submit Puzzle" button. There may also be a smaller reference image displayed above the grid to show you what the final completed picture should look like.

Analyze the reference image (if available) and examine the individual pieces in the tray. Look for visual continuities such as connecting lines, matching colors, geometric shapes, or distinct corners and edges that indicate where each piece belongs in the overall picture. 

To assemble the puzzle, use your mouse to drag a piece from the tray and drop it into the correct empty cell within the grid. Repeat this process for every piece until the tray is empty and the grid is full. If you realize a piece is in the wrong location, you can easily correct it by dragging the piece from its current grid cell back to the tray, or by dragging it directly into a different grid cell. 

Once all the pieces have been placed into the grid, take a moment to review the assembled image. Ensure that all visual elements align perfectly across the cell boundaries and that the final result matches the reference image or forms a coherent, continuous picture. When you are confident that the puzzle is correctly assembled, click the "Submit Puzzle" button to finalize your answer. Remember that you only have one attempt, so verify your arrangement thoroughly before submitting.

Structure_From_Motion.strategy:
To solve the Structure From Motion puzzle, read the on-screen prompt, which asks you to select all cells where the dots form a single rigid 3D object rotating smoothly in space.

Examine the grid of animated cells below. Each cell contains a cloud of dots moving against a dark background. These dots represent points on the surface of a 3D object. All cells in a given puzzle show the same underlying geometric shape, but the motion type differs between cells. Your task is not to identify the shape — it is to distinguish rigid from non-rigid motion.

In the correct cells, all dots will maintain fixed distances from each other as the object rotates, producing the visual impression of a solid, stable 3D body spinning smoothly. Look for coherent, synchronized rotation where the entire dot cloud moves as one unified structure without any internal deformation.

In the incorrect cells, the motion will exhibit one of several types of non-rigidity: the dots may wobble or oscillate around a shifting axis (axis wobble), parts of the dot cloud may pivot or hinge independently from other parts (articulated hinge), or dots may shuffle and jitter locally without maintaining consistent spatial relationships (local shuffle). These non-rigid motions will look unstable, jerky, or internally inconsistent compared to the smooth, steady rotation of the correct cells.

Watch each cell's animation for at least one full rotation cycle. Click on every cell that displays smooth, rigid rotation. After selecting all matching cells, click the "Submit" button to finalize your answer.

Subway_Paths.strategy: Read the text prompt above the grid carefully to identify the target number of valid routes required, the specific rule for allowed edge types (such as 'only ANIMAL stamps' or 'any stamp EXCEPT SHAPE'), and the provided examples of emojis that belong to each category. Next, inspect each subway map image displayed in the grid. In each map, locate the starting station, which is marked with a GREEN circle, and the destination station, which is marked with a RED circle. Examine the lines connecting the various stations; each edge features a specific emoji icon. Evaluate which edges are valid for travel by checking if their emoji falls into the allowed categories defined in the prompt. Trace all possible routes from the GREEN start station to the RED destination station using only these valid edges. Keep in mind that a valid route must be simple, meaning it cannot visit the same station more than once. Count the total number of valid routes available in the current map. If this count exactly matches the target number requested in the prompt, click on that map cell to select it. Repeat this path-finding and counting process for every map in the grid. Temporal_Object_Continuity.strategy:
To solve the Temporal Object Continuity puzzle, your objective is to find all cells where a moving object changes its identity while hidden behind an occluder.

Examine the grid of animated cells on the webpage. Each cell shows a geometric shape (such as a circle, square, triangle, star, or hexagon) of a specific color moving horizontally across the screen. Along its path, the shape passes behind one or more dark vertical bars (occluders) that temporarily hide it from view.

For each cell, carefully watch the object as it approaches and enters the occluder. Note both its shape and its color. Then observe what emerges from the other side. In a normal cell, the same shape with the same color will reappear. In a violating cell, the object will come out with a different shape AND a different color — for example, a red circle enters but a blue square exits. Both properties change simultaneously in violating cells.

Watch the full animation loop for every cell to ensure you catch any changes. There will typically be multiple violating cells per puzzle.
